tasks.short: Tell the sites how to apply our budget and booking rules.

today.trigger: A site manager or another unit asks how to treat a cost, a coding question or a budget overrun.
steps: Find the procedure on SharePoint and the budget line in AFAS Profit.
Check last time the same point was booked, usually in old Outlook mail.
Talk it through on Teams with the day-shift manager at Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo.
Write the answer by mail.
Answer the same point again when the next site asks.
drudgery: Searching old mail for the last wording.
Retyping the same explanation for each site.
Waiting while a site reconstructs the facts of the cost.
today.time_sinks: The back-and-forth to pin down the facts, and repeating one ruling across three sites.

lenses.faster: Searching SharePoint and old mail, and writing the first explanation, drop out, about a third of the time. The edit and the conversation stay, and they are most of what a question takes today.
lenses.autonomous: A question from a site or another unit starts it, and a draft is prepared from the procedure, the budget line and earlier rulings. The controller approves every answer before it is sent, and the finance director approves any answer that would change a budget or a limit.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift supervisors at Tilburg and Venlo get a written ruling in the same week, a group reached today only through the day-shift manager, and demand would grow because those questions already arise when the office is closed.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching old mail for the last explanation of a rule. The controller wants the exception call and the time with the site that is actually stuck.
lenses.options: Two drafts of the same overrun, one that lets the site proceed inside the limit and one that waits for the finance director, change whether the site commits the cost this week.
lenses.altitude: Fewer repeated mails, and a short register of rulings the sites can reuse. The controller gains the right to let a site proceed inside a written limit, and the expertise that grows is the exception that still reaches the desk.
reach: Finance Director: repeat explanations of an existing budget rule to the three site managers, while any change to the plan stays with the director.
FP&A Analyst: explaining a forecast line to a site manager, once the controller knows the labour, flex and transport drivers behind it.

tasks.human_edge: The controller knows which site will read a rule more widely than it was meant, and what the finance director has already promised. A pushed-back site manager is a conversation, and the CAO overtime or allowance behind the cost has to be read correctly.
tasks.pattern_why: The questions repeat, but the ruling depends on the site and on what has already been allowed. A draft shortens the reply. The controller stays the lead because the ruling is the work.

in_practice.trigger: A site, a night-shift supervisor or another unit asks how a cost or a budget exception should be treated.
steps: Pull the SharePoint procedure, the AFAS budget line and any earlier ruling on the same point.
Draft the answer with the rule, the facts and the proposed treatment.
The controller edits the judgement and sends it, or takes a budget change to the finance director.
File the ruling on the SharePoint register so the next site sees it.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves every answer before it goes out. The finance director approves any answer that changes a budget or a control limit.
data_needed: The question and the cost facts
Prior rulings on the same point
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint register of rulings, with the date and the approver.

evidence.claim: The Mercor month-end study did not measure client communication, asking the right questions, or building tacit context, and says the results do not mean accountants are replaceable.
On 160 US GAAP close tasks the leading row meets 61.8% of criteria and 58% of tasks are never fully solved; the bottleneck is accounting judgement.
No source in the digest shows a product that drafts Dutch budget rulings against AFAS and a SharePoint procedure set.

risks: A draft that sounds official can misstate a budget limit or a CAO allowance, and the site will act on it.
A ruling kept in a personal mailbox cannot be reused by the next site or shown to the auditor.
Night-shift questions often arrive with thin facts, so a fast answer on a wrong description is worse than waiting until the next morning.
research_questions: What share of policy questions in the last six months repeated a ruling already given?
Do site managers still wait for a conversation when a written answer is already clear?
Which answers would the finance director want to see before they go to a site?

tasks.short: Find where the operation makes or loses money, and what to change.

today.trigger: The monthly Power BI refresh, or a question from the finance director before the forecast meeting.
steps: Pull the AFAS extract and the Power BI views by site.
Rebuild an Excel bridge for labour, flex agencies, transport and other cost.
Compare with the forecast and the prior month.
Chase late agency invoices and miscoded lines with the bookkeepers.
Write a short note on what should change.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same workbook each month.
Aligning flex-agency invoices that arrive after the extract.
Fixing cost-centre codes before the numbers can be trusted.
today.time_sinks: The workbook itself, and the wait for agency cost that is not in AFAS yet.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the Excel bridge from the AFAS extract and Power BI drops out. Checking the draft causes and writing what should change stay, about half of the time this analysis takes now.
lenses.autonomous: The monthly Power BI refresh starts it, and in peak season a weekly flex pull starts a shorter version. The comparison and the first commentary run from the extract. The controller signs the note before it is used in the forecast or to change an agency order.
lenses.ambitious: Each week in peak season the three site managers get a call on whether to extend or cut flex-agency hours, a decision that today waits for the monthly forecast, and demand would grow when flex volume moves between 150 and 300 because that cost is committed before month-end.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the monthly workbook. The controller wants the hour spent on what the sites should change.
lenses.options: Reading the same flex spike as seasonal or as structural changes whether the agency order is cut for a week or the forecast is reset.
lenses.altitude: The week starts from a drafted variance note and moves to the two or three movements worth an action. The controller gains the right to put a flex-order recommendation in front of the sites before the forecast meeting, and the skill that grows is reading the operation.
reach: FP&A Analyst: the first-pass monthly commentary on the Power BI pack, once the controller uses the same forecast drivers for labour, flex and transport.

tasks.human_edge: The controller can tell a CAO allowance, a sick wave or a one-off customer deadline from a structural leak, and can judge what the site will actually change. That read sits outside the nightly extract.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack can be assembled on a schedule from AFAS and Power BI. Naming what the operation should change is advice the controller still leads, because the forecast has to be one the business will trust.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly Power BI refresh lands, and in peak season a weekly pull of flex hours by site is added.
steps: A saved comparison lines up AFAS actuals, the forecast and agency cost by site.
A draft note names the movements and a proposed cause, using site, shift and agency totals.
The controller checks the causes against what operations reported and marks which need a decision.
The note goes to the finance director and the three site managers.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller signs the note before it is used in the forecast or to change a flex order. Named employees and absence files stay out of the draft.
data_needed: Ledger actuals by site and cost type
CAO allowance rules at summary level, not per person
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint, stored with the Power BI snapshot date and the approver.

evidence.claim: Choi and Xie found accountants using AI closed the month 7.5 days faster across 79 small and mid-sized firms; 62% of 277 surveyed worry about errors.
On 160 US GAAP close tasks, 58% are never fully solved and the bottleneck is accounting judgement, which is the opportunity call in this task.
Noordhaven's flex cost can sit in three agency portals until the invoice is in AFAS, so a note built only on the nightly Power BI extract can be early.

risks: The 7.5-day result is the close at small and mid-sized firms, so it does not measure a weekly flex note at a 1,200-person logistics company.
Agency invoices that lag the hours will make a weekly margin look better or worse than the cash commitment already made.
Putting named staff, wage details or absence into the prompt would breach AVG; Wet verbetering poortwachter files do not belong in a margin note.
research_questions: How many days after the week ends do flex hours and agency invoices reach AFAS?
Which variances last year were large enough that a weekly flag would have changed an agency order?
Can a site manager cut flex hours, or does that authority sit with operations management?

tasks.short: Get the accounts through the audit and the Dutch filing rules.

today.trigger: The external auditor's planning memo or request list, on the year-end timetable.
steps: Agree scope and dates with the finance director and the audit firm.
Collect samples: invoices, Rabobank lines, contracts and journals.
Have the accountants and bookkeepers pull the underlying documents.
Walk through findings and draft the company's response.
Track open points until the opinion.
drudgery: Chasing sample copies.
Renaming and re-sending files the firm already holds.
Rebuilding tie-outs that were already done at the month close.
today.time_sinks: The weeks where the team hunts documents, ahead of any discussion of the findings.

lenses.faster: Collecting sample invoices, bank lines and contracts drops out, about a third of the time. The meetings, the findings and the sign-off stay, and they are about two thirds of this task.
lenses.autonomous: The auditor's request list, or the year-end close, starts it. Tie-out queries and the sample list run from AFAS and the Rabobank statements. The controller approves a reply or an adjustment before it goes out, and bank, AR and AP differences stay open until they are cleared or explained.
lenses.ambitious: The external auditor and the finance director get a quarterly tie-out of bank, AR, AP and VAT, a file they use today only at year-end, and demand would grow because interim findings are useful before the annual accounts are finished.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing sample copies through Outlook. The controller wants the findings meeting and the choice of which control to change.
lenses.options: A sample drawn by site, by staffing agency or by euro value changes which errors turn up and which finding the company has to answer for.
lenses.altitude: Audit weeks go to open differences and findings, with the sample list already built. The controller gains the right to issue the quarterly tie-out the firm works from, and the expertise that grows is which findings should change a control.
reach: Accountant: the first response to a routine sample request, once the controller knows the firm's standard list and the materiality they use.

tasks.human_edge: The controller judges what to concede, what is a real misstatement under BW 2 Titel 9, and how a finding will land with the finance director. The management representation stays a management act.
tasks.pattern_why: The sample list and the tie-out follow a checklist the team already knows. The open points are a conversation with the firm about judgement, and the controller leads that response.

in_practice.trigger: The auditor issues an interim or year-end request list, and the same tie-out also runs when the ledger closes.
steps: Saved queries tie Rabobank, AR and AP to the AFAS ledger and list what is still open.
A pack gives the samples, the differences and the query that produced them.
The controller reviews the differences and the draft replies.
Accountants add evidence a query cannot see, such as a contract.
The finance director agrees the response before it goes to the firm.
in_practice.human_gate: A reply is sent, and an adjustment is posted, only after the controller approves it. Unexplained bank, AR and AP differences stay on the list.
data_needed: Contracts and the prior-year finding list
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint audit folder: query name, extract date, sample list, response and approver.

evidence.claim: AFAS bank matching uses fixed rules on reference, IBAN and invoice number, so the unmatched remainder is the part people still clear.
The working pattern is that a draft does not count until bank, AR and AP tie out.
An estimate the auditor cannot rebuild fails when the prompt and the output sit in a personal account.
The published benchmarks are US GAAP. A Dutch statutory audit under BW 2 Titel 9 is untested.

risks: A tie-out that is green on the nightly extract and wrong against Rabobank will waste the auditor's visit.
The audit firm may refuse a sample log that lacks the query, the extract date and the approver.
US GAAP benchmark scores say nothing about Dutch law, the audit opinion or the management representation.
research_questions: What share of last year's auditor requests was already on the standard list from the year before?
Will the audit firm accept an AFAS tie-out export and a stored query as sample evidence, and what must the log contain?
How many findings were estimates, cut-off or classification, rather than a missing document?

tasks.short: Write the rules for budgets, cash, credit and the ledger.

today.trigger: A control failed, the auditor commented, or the procedure set comes up for its annual look.
steps: Read the SharePoint procedure and compare it with how AFAS is actually set.
Rewrite the change in Word.
Discuss the limit with the finance director.
Where the control checks staff expenses or overtime, decide what the works council must be told.
Publish the new version and tell the bookkeepers and the sites.
drudgery: Reformatting the old document.
Keeping competing versions in mail.
Chasing people to confirm they have read it.
today.time_sinks: The drafting and the circulation take longer than the decision on the limit.

lenses.faster: Writing the procedure up from a blank page drops out, a bit over half the time. Setting the limit, checking it against how the sites actually work, and publishing it stay.
lenses.autonomous: A control gap, an audit point or a scheduled review starts it, and a full draft is written from the current text and the AFAS settings. Publication waits for the controller, for the finance director where a mandate changes, and for the works-council step where staff expenses or overtime are checked.
lenses.ambitious: The three staffing agencies and the accounts-payable bookkeepers get a written hours-and-invoice control they lack today, and demand for an update would grow at each swing between 150 and 300 flex workers because the same points are re-agreed every peak.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reformatting last year's procedure. The controller wants the argument about the approval limit and who may commit flex cost.
lenses.options: A euro limit the site manager can approve alone, and a limit that also needs the controller, change who can commit flex and subcontract cost.
lenses.altitude: The week is a review of a drafted procedure and a decision on the limit, then publication. The controller gains the right to set the threshold sites and agencies work to, and the skill that deepens is the risk, the mandate and the evidence the rule leaves behind.
reach: Bookkeeper (accounts payable): the unwritten checks on a staffing-agency invoice, once the controller knows the portal fields and the AFAS payment-batch steps.

tasks.human_edge: The controller sets a limit this team of ten will follow and that still catches a bad payment, including an IBAN change on an agency. A control that watches staff expenses or overtime also has to be handled with the works council under the WOR.
tasks.pattern_why: A Noordhaven control note has fixed sections: scope, AFAS steps, approval limit, evidence and the exception path. One draft from the current text and the settings is a checkable document, and it takes effect only when the controller approves it.

in_practice.trigger: A control gap, an audit finding, or the scheduled review of the budget, cash, credit or accounting procedure.
steps: Collect the current SharePoint text and the AFAS approval, duplicate and IBAN settings.
Draft the procedure in the fixed sections.
The controller sets the limit and the exception path, and marks whether the works council must be informed.
The finance director agrees where the rule binds a signing mandate.
Publish on SharePoint and set AFAS to match the text.
in_practice.human_gate: The text is published, and the AFAS setting is changed, only after the controller approves. A control that checks individual staff expenses or overtime waits until the works-council step required by the WOR is done.
data_needed: AFAS approval limits, duplicate check and IBAN check
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history with approver and date, plus a pointer to the AFAS setting that matches it.

evidence.claim: Tax estimates and cash allocation need mandatory human review and approval, with timestamped logs.
An estimate the auditor cannot rebuild fails when the prompt and the output sit in a personal account.
No product in the digest writes Dutch internal-control procedures against AFAS mandates, IBAN checks and a works council.

risks: A polished draft can hide a limit that does not match the mandates already loaded in AFAS.
A control that monitors named employees can breach AVG, and an employment use of that kind needs a careful AI Act reading; the rule should stay on roles, euro limits and invoice fields.
Customer credit limits are a written AFAS rule. Letting a model set them on a customer file is a different decision from publishing the procedure.
research_questions: How many procedures changed last year because of a real control choice, and how many were wording only?
Which of those changes needed works-council information or consent under the WOR?
How often do agency invoices already fail the AFAS duplicate and IBAN checks?

tasks.short: Prepare the figures the fiscalist needs for the tax return.

today.trigger: The year is closed and the external fiscalist asks for the annual pack.
steps: Export the closed AFAS ledger, depreciation and VAT reports.
Build the commercial-to-fiscal bridge in Excel from last year's file.
List non-deductible costs, provisions and prior-year differences.
Send the pack and answer the fiscalist's questions.
Keep a copy with the tax file.
drudgery: Tying the bridge to the penny.
Reformatting last year's workbook.
Searching for the same correction that was made last year.
today.time_sinks: The bridge, and a second round of questions when a figure does not tie to the closed result.

lenses.faster: Pulling the totals and rebuilding last year's bridge drop out, about two fifths of the time. Reviewing the uncertain corrections and answering the fiscalist stay, about three fifths.
lenses.autonomous: Year-end close, or a quarterly check against the provisional assessment, starts it. The bridge is built from the AFAS export and stops when it does not tie to the closed result. The controller approves the pack before it goes to the fiscalist, who files the return.
lenses.ambitious: The external fiscalist gets a mid-year pack so the provisional corporate-tax assessment can be revised when the result moves, a decision today left until the annual file, and demand would grow in any year the result leaves the assessment because the cash tax is already set.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting last year's fiscal correction in an old workbook. The controller wants the uncertain items and the conversation with the fiscalist.
lenses.options: Treating a provision as deductible or leaving it out changes the taxable amount and whether a revised provisional assessment is worth the request.
lenses.altitude: The tax week becomes a review of a bridge that already ties, then the open items with the fiscalist. The controller gains the right to release the pack the return is built from, including a mid-year view of the assessment, and the fiscal judgement stays the expert core of the job.
reach: Accountant: the VAT summary that supports the annual figures, once the controller knows the AFAS VAT codes and how a suppletie is raised.

tasks.human_edge: The controller decides which costs are truly non-deductible, which position is uncertain enough to flag, and what Noordhaven will defend to the Belastingdienst. The company owns those facts. The fiscalist files.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack is one bridge from a closed ledger to a list of fiscal corrections, and it can be checked by tying it back. The controller approves it before it leaves. Dutch corporate tax and VAT were not in the US close benchmarks, so the output stays a draft with a gate.

in_practice.trigger: The annual ledger is closed and the fiscalist has asked for the pack, or a quarterly check against the provisional assessment is due.
steps: Export closed AFAS totals, depreciation, provisions and VAT codes.
Build the commercial-to-fiscal bridge with a source for each correction.
Stop when the bridge does not tie to the closed result.
The controller reviews the uncertain items and approves the pack.
Send it to the fiscalist, who prepares and files the return.
in_practice.human_gate: The controller approves the pack before it leaves the company. The draft does not file the return and does not change the provisional assessment.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint tax folder: extract date, bridge, approver and timestamp.

evidence.claim: Tax estimates need mandatory human review and approval, with timestamped logs.
AFAS cannot file the annual accounts of a large company with the KVK via SBR, and large companies must file that way from FY2025.
An estimate the auditor or the fiscalist cannot rebuild fails when the prompt and the output sit in a personal account.
Dutch corporate tax, the provisional assessment and VAT returns are outside the US GAAP benchmarks in the digest.

risks: A bridge that is one euro off the closed ledger will be rebuilt by the fiscalist, and the draft will have saved little.
The annual-accounts filing with the KVK is a separate act from the tax return. Mixing them up would send the wrong file down the wrong path.
A figure the fiscalist did not adopt can still leak into a forecast if the pack is treated as filed.
research_questions: Which sheets does the fiscalist still rebuild from the ledger, and which figures do they take as given?
How many fiscal corrections last year were a standing rule, and how many were a judgement?
Would a September pack have changed the provisional assessment in any of the last three years?
Does Noordhaven meet the large-company tests, and who files the SBR annual accounts with the KVK?

tasks.short: Plan the tax effect of investments, leases and provisions.

today.trigger: Budget season, a large investment or lease request, or a question from the finance director on a provision.
steps: Pull the ledger history and the fiscalist's last memo from SharePoint.
Sketch two or three treatments in Excel.
Discuss appetite and cash with the finance director.
Ask the fiscalist when the position is new.
Write the recommendation and file it.
drudgery: Redoing the same scenario maths.
Hunting the prior memo.
Formatting the comparison for the meeting.
today.time_sinks: Building the scenarios takes the time. The real work is the discussion of appetite and cash tax.

lenses.faster: Recalculating the treatments drops out, about a third of the time. The choice with the finance director, and with the fiscalist when the position is new, stays and is about two thirds.
lenses.autonomous: A capex or lease request above the threshold, or a direct question from the finance director, starts it. Up to three treatments are drafted with the effect on taxable result and on the provisional assessment. The finance director accepts one before anyone acts, after the fiscalist has seen a position the company has not taken before.
lenses.ambitious: A fleet, racking or fit-out request above the threshold carries a fiscal and cash consequence while it is still open, a look today saved for the autumn tax meeting, and demand would grow because the sites raise these requests all year.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss recalculating the same three treatments in Excel. The controller wants the recommendation on timing and cash, made with the finance director.
lenses.options: Buy this year, lease, or defer to next year changes the cash, the depreciation and the tax the finance director is about to commit to.
lenses.altitude: Planning starts from three tied scenarios on a live request. The controller gains the right to put the tax and cash consequence on that request before the finance director commits, and the expertise that grows is the structuring choice.
reach: FP&A Analyst: the tax line in the annual forecast, once the controller can show the cash effect of the provisional assessment inside that model.

tasks.human_edge: The controller, with the fiscalist, judges the company's appetite for a position the Belastingdienst may challenge, and the cash effect of changing the provisional assessment. That appetite is a management decision.
tasks.pattern_why: The treatments can be calculated and tied to the ledger. The choice depends on appetite, cash and what the company is willing to defend, so the controller and the finance director stay in the lead.

in_practice.trigger: A buy or lease request crosses the agreed euro threshold, or the finance director asks for a tax view on a provision.
steps: Pull the handbook life, the fiscalist's last position and the current provisional assessment.
Draft at most three treatments with taxable result and cash tax.
The controller reviews the drafts and marks any position the company has not taken before.
The finance director chooses, after the fiscalist has seen a new position.
File the chosen treatment with the request.
in_practice.human_gate: No treatment is acted on until the finance director accepts it. A new position goes to the external fiscalist before it is used.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint tax folder, attached to the capex or lease request, with the choice and the approver.

evidence.claim: Tax estimates and cash allocation require mandatory human review and approval, with timestamped logs.
The Mercor study did not measure asking the right questions or building tacit context, which is what a planning conversation is.
Dutch investment deductions, fiscal depreciation and Belastingdienst practice are not tested in the digest's US GAAP material.

risks: A scenario the company follows without the fiscalist can create a position nobody can defend later.
Moving a provisional assessment on a draft changes cash before the finance director has accepted the risk.
A memo that lives in a personal account cannot be shown to the fiscalist or the Belastingdienst a year later.
research_questions: Which tax memos in the last two years changed a lease, a purchase date or a provision?
Above what amount does the finance director want a fiscal scenario attached to a request?
Which of those scenarios does the external fiscalist already provide under the current engagement?

tasks.short: Set depreciation lives and advise on buy, lease or sell.

today.trigger: A new asset, a lease proposal, a disposal, or the monthly depreciation review.
steps: Check the asset class, method and life on the AFAS asset.
Recalculate the charge in Excel when the class or the life is blank.
For a larger item, compare buy, lease and sell.
Advise the finance director.
Tell the accountants what to post.
drudgery: Assets with a blank life.
A spreadsheet copy of a charge the asset register could compute.
One-off journals that then have to be tied back.
today.time_sinks: The annual clean-up of the register, and the exceptions, take the hours. The routine charge is the smaller part.

lenses.faster: Calculating the charge for every asset that already has a class drops out, about half the time. Approving the batch, setting a life for a new class, and the buy, lease or sell conversation stay.
lenses.autonomous: Month-end, a capitalised invoice, or a lease or sale proposal starts it. AFAS applies the handbook method, life and residual to every asset with a class and lists the rest. The controller approves the journal after it ties to the register, and approves a new life or a lease classification before it is stored.
lenses.ambitious: Once a month the finance director and the site managers get a redeploy-or-sell call on idle trailers and forklifts above a book-value threshold, a look today taken at budget time, and demand would grow in peak season when one site is short and another is idle.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the spreadsheet copy of the depreciation run. The controller wants the buy, lease or sell advice on the few assets large enough to matter.
lenses.options: Buy, lease, or move an idle trailer or forklift from another site changes the cash leaving the business and the depreciation the forecast will carry.
lenses.altitude: Known classes run from the handbook after a batch approval, and the remaining work is new lives and the larger capital choices. The controller gains the right to set the life for a class and to hold a journal that does not tie to the register, which is a deeper capital judgement.
reach: Accountant: the monthly depreciation journal and the check that it ties to the asset register, once the controller knows the AFAS fixed-asset posting steps.

tasks.human_edge: Useful life and residual value of a specialised asset, such as cold-store fit-out or a custom trailer, are a judgement, as is whether a contract is a lease under the relevant RJ. A changed life needs a reason the auditor can read.
tasks.pattern_why: Method, life and residual value by asset class are rules, and AFAS can apply them the same way every month to a charge that must match the register. The controller approves the batch, and approves every new life and every lease classification.

in_practice.trigger: The depreciation run is due, a capitalised invoice arrives without a class, or a buy, lease or sell proposal crosses the threshold.
steps: AFAS applies the handbook method, life and residual value to every asset that has a class.
The run lists assets with no class, a proposed life change, or a charge that does not tie to the register.
The controller approves the journal once the register ties.
Above the threshold, a short note compares buy, lease and redeploy, and the controller advises the finance director.
in_practice.human_gate: The journal is posted only after it ties to the register and the controller approves the batch. A new useful life or a lease classification is approved by the controller before it is stored on the asset.
data_needed: Asset register with class, method, life and residual
Lease contracts and net book value
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS asset master holds the rate. SharePoint holds the reason for a life change and any buy, lease or sell note, with the approver.

evidence.claim: SAP's accruals agent prepares journals for an accountant to accept, adjust or reject, advises at most five expense categories per handbook, and does not run on AFAS.
Trintech's accruals agent drafts and rolls forward accruals, flags outliers, and keeps a Review and Approve step plus Retain for Audit.
A drafted amount should not be posted until the related tie-out is clean. For this task the tie-out is the asset register.
Whether AFAS already posts depreciation from the asset master at Noordhaven, and how Dutch useful-life judgement will be audited, is not settled by the US GAAP benchmarks.

risks: If AFAS already posts from the asset master, a second calculation will create the differences it was meant to remove.
A life change that flatters the month will be the first item the auditor asks to rebuild.
Vendor accrual agents are narrow and are not an AFAS fixed-asset subledger. Copying their scope onto depreciation rates would overstate what they do.
research_questions: Does AFAS already calculate depreciation from method and life on the asset, and which assets still need a manual journal?
How many useful lives were changed in the last two years, and what reason did the auditor accept?
Did any buy-versus-lease note in that period change a decision above the finance director's threshold?

role.altitude: The controller moves from building the month to designing the rules the month runs on: accrual handbook, asset lives, approval limits, the tax bridge and the tie-outs. The week goes to exceptions, the forecast the sites will recognise, and the auditor. The judgement gets deeper, and the assembly shrinks.
reach: FP&A Analyst: first-pass monthly variance commentary, and the tax line in the forecast, once the controller uses the same drivers for labour, flex, transport and the provisional assessment.
Accountant: the monthly depreciation journal, the VAT bridge for the annual pack, and the first reply to a routine audit sample.
Bookkeeper (accounts payable): the unwritten checks on staffing-agency invoices, once they are written into the control procedure and matched in AFAS.
Finance Director: repeat explanations of an existing budget rule to Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, while any change to the plan stays with the director.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks are about 280 hours a year, under a fifth of the role. The close itself, the forecast meetings, cash allocation and signing sit outside the list and remain. Dutch GAAP judgement, the tax position and what the finance director will sign cap how far the slice can run unattended. Hours freed here shorten the pack. Where a control watches staff expenses or overtime, the works council's right to be informed or to consent sets the pace.
skills_to_grow: An accrual handbook and materiality thresholds the team and the auditor can reperform.
Tie-out queries on the AFAS ledger for bank, debtors, creditors, VAT and fixed assets, and how to read the nightly Power BI snapshot.
Dutch GAAP (BW 2 Titel 9 and the relevant RJ) at the level of a useful life, a lease and an estimate.
The fiscalist's commercial-to-tax bridge, the VAT codes and the provisional assessment.
What a log must hold so a draft can be rebuilt a year later outside any personal account.
CAO cost at summary level, so a site margin is not read as if overtime and flex were the same as contracted hours.
role.ambitious_version: The controller keeps a close that ties out before a journal is posted, and during peak season each site manager gets a weekly call on flex hours and overtime against margin, in time to change the agency order. A material investment still open carries a lease-or-buy and tax consequence for the finance director. The external auditor works from a quarterly tie-out, and the fiscalist gets a pack that can move the provisional assessment when the year is off track. The test is fewer days to close, a forecast the business trusts, and fewer audit adjustments.
